title: Do door robots that learn from their own costs keep honouring an urgency cue?
summary: society-cheapcue gave robots a fixed rule (yield to someone sending the urgency cue, go against everyone else) that cost the robots themselves 0.29 per encounter. Here each robot learns its own go probability for cue senders (gS) and others (gQ) by a logit response to its own expected cost, with people re-equilibrating (30% robots, 20% urgent people, normal cue cost 0.6, collision cost 3, waiting and dithering cost 1). The fleet keeps honouring the cue (gS gS ≤ 0.03 in every cellle; 0.04 in every cell) but stops going against everyone else: gQ settles at 0.18 (ρ = 1) to 0.42 (ρ = 0), not 1, from three different starts. The urgent people's gain over yield-all shrinks to −0.005 at ρ = 0.25 (a small loss) and is positive (+0.18) only at ρ = 0; the crowd is still worse off than under yield-all in every setting tried (+0.006 to +0.065). A sharper robot response (logit 32) goes against others only 0.14 of the time. Assumed, not sourced: ρ, cue costs, logit sharpness, round-figure door costs, mean-field people, random pairing; robot learning is a fixed point of the response, not a simulated learning run.
lede: do door robots that learn from their own costs keep honouring an urgency cue? They keep yielding to cue senders but stop going against everyone else, which erases most of the cue's gain to urgent people.
